title: Mitigating Resource Contention for Responsive On-device Machine Learning Inferences
problem: On-device ML inference frameworks suffer from performance degradation under resource contention due to static and coarse-grained resource allocation in dynamic embedded system environments.
motivation: Responsive ML inference on edge devices requires adaptation to unpredictable resource availability and load fluctuations.
method: FlexOn framework combines fine-grained model segmentation with dynamic resource selection to rapidly adapt to runtime conditions. The framework selects execution segments based on available resources, utilizing both local and external compute as needed.
key_novelty: First work addressing resource contention in open embedded systems for better ML inference responsiveness.
contributions: Fine-grained model segmentation enabling flexible execution strategies
Dynamic resource selection mechanism adapting to runtime availability
54% average latency and 58% tail latency improvement across embedded platforms
limitations: Evaluation limited to three embedded platforms; specific to on-device inference scenarios.
primary_theme: Dynamic resource adaptation for responsive on-device inference
